en: Points of Controversy:
The Refutation Section,
Chapter Sixteen.
The Discourse on Suppression:
Does one suppress the mind of another? Yes.
Does one restrain another’s mind, thinking, “May you not be lustful,” “May you not be hateful,” “May you not be deluded,” “May you not be defiled”?
One should certainly not say so … [and so on] … Does one restrain another’s mind?
“Yes,” you say.
But can it be said that one person restrains another’s arisen contact so that it “may not cease”?
Certainly not; such should not be said …pe…
Another person’s arisen feeling … [and so on] … arisen perception … arisen volition …
arisen consciousness … arisen faith … arisen energy …
Does one restrain arisen mindfulness... arisen concentration...
[and so on]... arisen wisdom, thinking, "May it not cease"?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does one person restrain the mind of another? Yes.
Does one abandon lust for the sake of another’s welfare?
Does one abandon hatred? ... [and so on] ...
does one abandon lack of moral dread?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … One person restrains the mind of another? Yes.
Does one develop the path for the sake of another’s welfare?
… does one develop the foundations of mindfulness? … pe … does one develop the factors of enlightenment?
It should not be said so … [as before] … One person restrains the mind of another? Yes.
Does one person fully understand suffering for the sake of another, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, and develop the path?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Does one person restrain the mind of another?
“Yes,” you say.
“One person is the doer for another; one person makes happiness or suffering created by another, and another experiences it?
You should not speak thus… [and so on].
"One restrains another's mind"?
Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“By oneself alone is evil done;
by oneself is one defiled.
By oneself is evil not done;”
One is purified by oneself alone;
purity and impurity are personal;
no one can purify another.
Is that indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
"One restrains another's mind.
Is it not the case that one should say, "One restrains another's mind"?
“Yes.
“But is it not the case that there are those who have attained strength and those who have attained mastery?
“Yes.”
If there are those who have attained strength and those who have attained mastery, then indeed, O sir, it must be said:
"One person restrains the mind of another.
The Discussion on Restraint is finished.
